value.rationale: The critical KPP Hardy boundary is a naturally motivated threshold: any fixed finite attractive defect destroys nonnegativity. This finding sharply quantifies the emergent negative eigenvalue at logarithmic scale, reveals universality over arbitrary defect positions via ground-state-weighted mass, and proves eventual uniqueness, distinguishing the critical response from the supercritical inverse-square spectral accumulation.
